notas:
I checked the methods before deciding the reports are linked correctly. The SJAR article (Alvarez2006, principal) used two Class A pans at the UPCT Experimental Station, Cartagena (37°35'N, 0°59'W), with an insulated, balance-weighed pan and an always-open reference pan. Runs were 10 days per configuration in May-June 2003, with single and double black PE (1-BPE, 2-BPE). The thesis (JM2009) chapter 8 used the same station and the same shaded/reference Class A pan pair, with experiment dates in May 2003. It extends the same series to seven shade materials. The thesis is therefore not independent.

The thesis 2BPE row (row 2, S = 0.835, SD 2.3%) duplicates principal row 2 (0.835, SD 0.023) exactly, so it is not added. The thesis BPE row (row 1) is the same condition as principal row 1, with a value conflict (0.731 vs 0.751): keep 0.751.

The five other materials (rows 3-7: WPE, 2WPE, GPE, ALU, BLPE) are added as distinct conditions of the same experiment. Their run length and exact dates are not recoverable: the local text file for JM2009 is a scanned PDF with no text layer (only 'reproduced with permission' lines), so period_days stays null. Their water area is 1.14 m2 vs 1.15 m2 in the principal; both come from the standard Class A diameter, so harmonise to 1.15 m2.

These seven materials were probably also published as Martinez-Alvarez et al. 2006, Agric. Water Manage. 84, 229-239 (efficiency of shading materials). That paper is not in textos_txt. If it enters the corpus it must join this group, and its Table values should replace the thesis values as the peer-reviewed source. The Alvarez2010 SJAR full-scale reservoir study (group Cartagena_reservoir_shade_cloth) is a different experiment and correctly sits outside this group.

Its 12 rows (Stage 1 rows 1-5 and Stage 2 rows 6-12) repeat principal rows 4, 5, 1, 2, 3, 16, 17, 11, 12, 13, 14 and 15 with identical E_o, E_c and S, so they are duplicates.
